INTELLIGENCE ASSESSMENT: RUSSIAN MILITARY POSTURE IN THE CAUCASUS

Date: 10 March 2026
Classification: UNCLASSIFIED
Source Reliability: C3

KEY JUDGMENTS

It is assessed as LIKELY (0.70-0.80) that Russia is reinforcing its military presence in the North Caucasus Military District in preparation for increased power projection into the South Caucasus. General Valery Gerasimov, Chief of the General Staff, has reportedly ordered the redeployment of the 58th Combined Arms Army from its garrison at Vladikavkaz to forward positions near the Georgian border.

SITUATION

On 3 March 2026, satellite imagery from Maxar Technologies revealed increased activity at Mozdok Airbase in North Ossetia, including the deployment of Su-34 fighter-bombers and Il-76 transport aircraft. The 4th Air and Air Defence Forces Command has established a forward air operations center at the base.

Russian Defense Minister Andrei Belousov met with Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan in Yerevan on 5 March 2026 to discuss the status of Russian military facilities in Armenia, specifically the 102nd Military Base in Gyumri and the 3624th Air Base at Erebuni. Armenia has signaled intent to diversify its security partnerships, holding joint military exercises with NATO member France in January 2026.

Turkey, a NATO ally, has expressed concern through Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan that increased Russian military activity could destabilize the Nagorno-Karabakh ceasefire brokered by Moscow in 2020. Azerbaijan's President Ilham Aliyev held a phone call with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan on 8 March 2026 to coordinate diplomatic positions.

IMPLICATIONS

The IRGC's Quds Force has reportedly increased liaison activity with Russian military intelligence (GRU) in Damascus, Syria, suggesting coordination between Moscow and Tehran on broader regional objectives. This is assessed as ROUGHLY EVEN CHANCE (0.40-0.55).

The European Union has called for de-escalation, with EU High Representative Josep Borrell issuing a statement from Brussels on 9 March 2026.
